title: Moment representations for positive functionals on countably normed algebras
statement: Fix the convention that \(A\) is a commutative unital complex Fr\'echet \(*\)-algebra: its topology is Hausdorff, complete and defined by countably many norms, multiplication is jointly continuous, and the involution is continuous. Let \(X_h(A)\) be its continuous unital Hermitian characters with the weak topology. Characterize those \(A\) for which every continuous complex-linear functional \(L\) satisfying \(L(a^*a)\ge0\) for every \(a\in A\) has a finite positive Radon measure \(\mu_L\) on \(X_h(A)\) such that \(L(a)=\int\chi(a)\,d\mu_L(\chi)\) for all \(a\in A\). All character evaluations in this identity must be integrable. This is a universal property of the algebra, not a question about one chosen \(L\).
status: November 2026: this entry records a precise editorial version of the notebook's axiomatization programme. Known nuclear-space and moment criteria cover specified subclasses and individual functionals; the opened sources do not characterize the universal property above. No claim that this exact reconstruction is a recognized unresolved conjecture is made.

title: The unextended semisimple Gelfand--Kirillov conjecture
statement: For a complex semisimple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\), is \(\operatorname{Frac}U(\mathfrak g)\) isomorphic to \(D_{|\Phi^+|,\operatorname{rank}\mathfrak g}\) without extending the centre?
status: November 2026: false in general by Premet (2009 preprint; 2010 publication), true for type A. The cited 2013 source leaves C and G2 open; no later exact resolution was verified. The 1969 theorem after central extension is a different assertion.

title: Automorphisms of Weyl division rings
statement: Describe the automorphism groups of Weyl division rings; in the present occurrence, determine \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Frac}A_1(\mathbb C)\), keeping polynomial algebra automorphisms and rational-subfield stabilizers distinct.
status: November 2026: no complete description was found in this audit; Dumas explicitly records the full automorphism-group question as open. The known stabilizer of \(\mathbb C(q)\) consists of lifted fractional-linear maps and rational shears. Lauritzen--Thomsen's October/November 2026 theorem on equality of left/right indices is a different result and does not settle the automorphism classification.

title: A universal family for the elliptic moduli problem
statement: Does an ordinary complex analytic parameter space represent all pointed elliptic families up to isomorphism, and what construction retains a universal family when this fails?
status: November 2026: the unrigidified family functor is not represented by the coarse j-line. A full homology marking gives the upper-half-plane universal family; the quotient stack or Mumford moduli site retains automorphisms. These facts were already established before the seminar.
